correctness.rationale: A fiber with two endpoints cannot map to a target vertex adjacent to another occupied target vertex; mixed images therefore force injectivity and a bipartition-oriented inverse. Independent images admit arbitrary disjoint singleton/cross-edge fibers; a continuous section exists exactly if forced singleton sources occur on at most one source side. The multinomial and falling-factorial formulas partition all maps without overlap. The idempotent formula fixes each image vertex and counts only optional opposite-side partners. Exhaustive distinct continuity/section/idempotence checks on seven graphs, plus explicit full-semigroup witnesses on small cases, agreed.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite graphs are a natural two-parameter family containing induced four-cycles and strong matching structure. The exact description of nonregular elements has a sharp rank cutoff and yields three full rank enumerators for total, nonregular, and idempotent populations; these are natural independent invariants useful in comparing and sampling full graph-continuous transformation monoids. This is a nontrivial full population classification beyond a one-sided star count, with no unsupported broader complexity claims.
